newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow police say they unfroze $56.81 mln MinFins.
newsitem.headline: Moscow police say they unfroze $56.81 mln MinFins.

text.p: A Moscow detective said on Thursday he had issued an order to unfreeze $56.81 million of Russian MinFin bonds which he had frozen in June.

Mikhail Ignatyev, a detective in the investigations department of the 5th central Moscow police precinct, told Reuters he was acting on the instructions of a district prosecutor in Moscow's Tagansk district.
The prosecutor had previously ordered the bonds to be frozen during the summer.

On Wednesday Prosecutor-General Yuri Skuratov ordered a review of all cases where MinFin bonds had been frozen, and said the securities should be freed if necessary if they had been acquired in good faith.
An aide to Skuratov said the Tagansk prosecutor had already ordered the release of some $21 million of bonds.
It appeared that this $21 million of bonds was part of the $56.81 million released by Ignatyev, but it was not immediately possible to confirm this.
The $56.81 million would represent most of the affected bonds.
In July the finance ministry detailed some $24 million of bonds which were frozen. As $6.93 million were on both lists the total known to have been frozen was about $74 million.
